title: Clermont-Ferrand Weather Forecast and Climate Guide
content:
## Temperature

The climate in Clermont-Ferrand is characterised by notable seasonal temperature fluctuations. Throughout the year, residents and visitors can feel both the chill of winter months and the warmth of summer days. The coldest month is usually January, when the average temperature is about 3.4°C, with night lows dropping on average to 0.5°C, and day highs around 6.3°C. In contrast, the hottest month is August, with an average temperature of 19.8°C; during this period, daytime temperatures often reach 25.3°C, and night temperatures drop to a comfortable 14.3°C. [...] Summer months in Clermont-Ferrand, especially July and August, offer pleasantly warm weather, ideal for walking and getting to know the city. Average daily highs during this period range from 22.9°C in June to 25.3°C in August. Evenings and nights bring refreshing coolness as the temperature drops noticeably, falling on average to 12-14°C. Such diurnal variations make summer evenings particularly comfortable after a relatively warm day. [...] In the summer months (June-August), when the average temperature reaches 17-20°C and the maximum is about 25°C, you will need light clothes: t-shirts, shorts, dresses. However, do not forget a light jacket or cardigan for evening walks. Sunscreen and a hat will also be relevant. In spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November), the weather is cooler, with average temperatures from 7°C to 16°C. During this period, it is worth taking sweaters, jeans, a mid-season jacket, and possibly a scarf. In winter (December-February), the average temperature hovers around 3-5°C, so a warm jacket, hat, gloves, and warm layers will be absolutely necessary for a comfortable stay.

![Flag - France](../../images/flags/France.png "Flag - France")

![Climate chart - Clermont Ferrand](/images/charts/Clermont-Ferrand-France.png "Climate chart - Clermont Ferrand")

The climate of Clermont-Ferrand is **temperate**, cold enough in winter and warm in summer, but with some continental characteristics.

The city is located in south-central France, in Auvergne, at the foot of the Chaîne des Puys (a chain of volcanoes arranged from north to south, whose highest peak reaches 1,465 meters or 4,800 feet), and northeast of the Massif Central.

The altitude of the city ranges from 330 to 500 meters (1,080 to 1,650 feet). The airport, where the weather station is located, is at 330 meters (1,080 ft).

![Clermont-Ferrand](/images/Clermont-Ferrand.jpg "Clermont-Ferrand")

The mountains reduce the influence of the Atlantic, so the climate in Clermont-Ferrand is a little more arid and continental than in other cities in south-central France.

Clermont-Ferrand is one of the driest cities in France, and is only beaten by a few cities in the south (Perpignan, Leucate, Aix-en-Provence, Marseille).

## Winter

The **winter** is quite cold. There may be relatively mild periods, when Atlantic currents prevail. There may also be cold and humid periods, in which fogs and low clouds form, and other colder periods, when the temperature drops below freezing.

Sometimes, there can be **cold spells**, in which temperatures can drop as low as -10 °C (14 °F) or even below.

The coldest record is -29 °C (-20.2 °F) and was set in February 1929.

## Summer

In **summer**, the temperatures are generally pleasant and lend themselves to outdoor activities, although sometimes there can be rains and thunderstorms.
